summary: Off-peak EU batch embeddings occasionally routed to US dedicated pool causing large p95 latency regressions
description: Issue summary: Customer runs recurring off-peak batch embedding jobs in eu-west-1 on a Dedicated pool. During the nightly window (23:30-02:00 UTC) a subset of jobs that start in EU are observed to make requests routed to our us-east-1 dedicated pool, introducing ~600-900ms extra p95 latency per request and extra egress/egress-costs. Impact: customer reported increased overall job completion time (up to 30%) and billing anomalies due to cross-region egress. Environment: Dedicated capacity, tenant-specific reserved pool, batch job runner using SDK v1.4.2. Expected behavior: jobs pinned to EU dedicated capacity for entire run when customer uses residency=dedicated and pool pinning. Observed behavior: routing drifts to US mid-run for some long-running batches.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer schedules a long-running batch embedding job (500k embeddings) targeting eu-west-1 reserved pool with residency=pinned and pool_id provided.
2) Job launches at 23:45 UTC and begins processing; initial requests served from eu-west-1 nodes (confirmed by IP and edge headers).
3) After ~18-30 minutes into the job, subset of worker requests show backend-edge headers with us-east-1 edge and serving IPs.
4) Customer observes p95 latency climb and notices additional egress entries in billing report crossing region boundary.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 02:00 - Triage: Correlated customer report with autoscaler activity on eu-west-1 dedicated pool during nightly maintenance window.
Observed control-plane decision logs indicating a fallback to us-east-1 with reason 'insufficient_capacity' and 'drain' flags on eu-west nodes.

Autoscaler traces show spike in 'scale_down' activities between 23:50-00:10 UTC followed by rapid 'scale_up' attempts; cooldown policies allowed transient period where available capacity for pinned pools dipped below request demand.

Router policy for pinned pools has a soft-fallback path that can route to compatible dedicated pools when pinned pool cannot satisfy request and 'strict_residency' is not enforced; customer believed pool pinning would be strict by default for Dedicated tenants.
No evidence of SDK misconfiguration on customer side; their pool_id was set in job config and authenticated token scoped correctly.
comments: Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-13: Thanks for the report — I can see the routing lines that moved to us-east. We're opening this with SRE to validate autoscaler behavior and control-plane decisioning.

Customer (SustainAI - Alex Romero) 2026-03-13: We configured pool_id and assumed pinning would prevent cross-region egress. This is causing overnight job latency spikes and unexpected billing. Please advise.

SRE (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-14: Assigning to routing/autoscaler teams. Initial hypothesis: dedicated autoscaler cooldown allowed transient capacity dip; control-plane allowed fallback to preserve throughput. Need to confirm policy defaults for 'pinned' jobs on Dedicated contracts.

Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-14: Temporary workaround provided to customer: set strict_residency=true in job metadata OR schedule jobs in a shorter window to avoid autoscale events. Customer testing now.
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-14: Created linked INT ticket for autoscaler policy review (INT-4421).
workaround: Short-term: Re-run jobs with strict_residency=true or specify explicit reserved_pool_id and increase min_replicas for the reserved pool before the job window. Alternatively schedule batch to avoid autoscaler churn window (start before 23:30 UTC).
resolution: In Progress - engineering is evaluating autoscaler cooldown and control-plane fallback policies. Plan: make pinned-pool fallback opt-in for Dedicated customers and provide clearer contract-level knob (strict_residency).
